content.comment_body: Hello, I'm looking for advice on controlling sensors with my [product_name]. I've checked previous discussions and found I might need an [product_name] expansion module, but I'm unclear which one to purchase. Since it's a significant expense if I choose incorrectly, any guidance would be appreciated. I've been researching products on [url]. Thank you, [user_name].

You can use most types of sensors with the [product_name]. Important note: On the basic DC version of [product_name], only sensors with up to 10 Volt output are compatible. Most sensors offer 0 - 10 Volt outputs, and these can be directly connected (only for DC version). For sensors with 0 or 4 - 20 mA output, you have two options: place a 500 Ohm resistor between the analog input and ground to generate the correct voltage signal for direct connection, or use an [product_name] analog input module, which attaches to the side of the basic unit. The basic version provides 2 or 4 analog inputs depending on settings in the software, but analog inputs cannot be used as digital inputs simultaneously. The analog module supports PT100, 0-10 Volt, or 0/4-20 mA sensors based on the chosen software setting, and has two analog inputs available. There is also a module for PT1000 sensors (possibly the [product_name] RTD module, though I'm not certain).

analysis.insight_summary: Users need help integrating multiple environmental sensors (such as those for temperature, humidity, pH, and EC/PPM) with the [product_name] system. The discussion centers around compatibility between sensor output types and the required hardware modules. Uncertainty about which modules to use and input voltage requirements has led to confusion and concern over making costly mistakes, affecting user confidence in making purchasing decisions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward instructions for selecting compatible sensors and input modules for their [product_name] system so that they can avoid unnecessary expenses and ensure everything works as intended.
